newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile shares end higher, power sector sparkles.
newsitem.headline: Chile shares end higher, power sector sparkles.

text.p: Bucking Wall Street's slide, Chilean blue chips surged to a strong close on heavy foreign demand for key electricity stocks, said dealers.
"The demand for ADRs prevented the IPSA index from falling," said one broker.

The rally is seen continuing at the opening, although much will depend on the flow of buy orders from New York, they said. The 40-share index ended up 0.96 percent at 114.67 points. The general index gained 0.42 percent to 5,297.64 points.
Turnover fell slightly to 10.4 billion pesos.
Electricity shares, which account for a 40 percent weighting in the IPSA index, surged for a variety of reasons, said dealers.
Top gainer Chilgener rose on a scramble by investors to buy shares before the closing date next week to register for the company's forthcoming stock split, they said.
Chilgener ended up 2.42 percent at 2,755 pesos.
Endesa rose on speculation that the company will report strong first quarter earnings because of higher than expected non-operating gains, said dealers.
The company, which has dollar-denominated debts, is seen benefitting from the revaluation of the peso earlier this year.
Endesa closed up 2.05 percent to 261-1/2 pesos. Its holding company Enersis rose 1.39 percent to 256 pesos.
Losers included fising company Eperva, down 4.76 percent at 100 pesos and steel-maker Cap which shed 0.1 percent to 970 pesos.
